changes.before: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April indicates that the pace of improvement in the labor market has slowed while growth in economic activity appears to have picked up. Although the unemployment rate has declined, job gains have diminished.
changes.after: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market strengthened and that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate rate. Job gains were strong in June following weak growth in May.
On balance, payrolls and other labor market indicators point to some increase in labor utilization in recent months.
Near-term risks to the economic outlook have diminished.

changes.before: Growth in household spending has strengthened.
changes.after: Household spending has been growing strongly but business fixed investment has been soft.

changes.before: Market-based measures of inflation compensation declined;
changes.after: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low;
Voting against the action was Esther L. George, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.

parsed.rationale: The statement upgrades its labor market assessment, adds that near-term risks have diminished, and records a hawkish dissent favoring a hike, all pointing toward an earlier rate increase. Forward guidance and the policy rate are unchanged, so the shift is moderately rather than strongly hawkish.

spans.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in April indicates that the pace of improvement in the labor market has slowed while growth in economic activity appears to have picked up. Although the unemployment rate has declined, job gains have diminished.
Growth in household spending has strengthened.
Market-based measures of inflation compensation declined;

Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market strengthened and that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate rate. Job gains were strong in June following weak growth in May.
On balance, payrolls and other labor market indicators point to some increase in labor utilization in recent months.
Near-term risks to the economic outlook have diminished.
Household spending has been growing strongly but business fixed investment has been soft.
Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low;
Voting against the action was Esther L. George, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
